title: Legal work, without limits
summary: Legora is the collaborative AI powering lawyers to review and research faster, draft smarter, and advise with precision. Legora adapts to your ways of working, unlocking team and machine collaboration at scale.
body_markdown:
Every in-house team has work it would take on with more capacity. A policy that needs updating. Agreements that deserve a closer look. A product initiative that would benefit from legal advice before a line of code is written. Instead, teams have had to make trade-offs. For years, the time needed to complete a task, or cost of engaging with outside counsel have constrained what legal teams can achieve.


Then there are the systems and software lawyers use to do the work. Legal intake is tracked in a spreadsheet, contracts live in another tool, spend in a third. Each tool imposes its own limitations on how the work should be executed and managed.


AI is beginning to change that equation. As more work becomes feasible, legal teams have an opportunity to rethink how the work is done, where they can deliver even more business value and how they should organize themselves to deliver it. At Legora, we call that ambition **legal work, without limits** : helping legal teams take on work that was previously out of reach, and shape it around how the team actually works instead of the limits of each tool.


## When more legal work becomes possible


Much of the discussion about legal AI starts with time savings. Those gains matter but their broader significance is what they make worth doing. If reviewing an agreement takes less time, a team can examine a larger share of its contracts. If approved policy guidance becomes easier to access, colleagues can get help at the point of making a decision. If monitoring regulations requires less manual work, a periodic exercise could become a more regular part of how the business manages change.


Our view is that legal will experience a version of Jevons’ Paradox: as the cost of doing work falls, demand for it grows. Lower costs, shorter waits and easier access will encourage businesses to seek more legal support.


AI adoption across other functions will also accelerate business activity. As the business moves faster, legal teams have an opportunity to bring their expertise to more business-critical decisions as strategic partners. Capturing that opportunity depends on whether in-house teams can move to AI-native ways of working.


## Learnings from software engineering


Software engineering gives us an early indication of where legal work is heading. At Legora, coding agents increasingly complete substantial pieces of work, and we are seeing huge productivity gains per engineer. Internal data shows that between July and October 2026, our engineers have more than tripled the number of code changes shipped to production.


We expect legal to follow a similar trajectory as the capabilities needed for legal work mature. Our recent[in-house ROI report](https://legora.com/roi-in-house) points the same way, with 80% of participants reporting that they are accomplishing more in the same amount of time when using Legora, with 77% reallocating that saved time to higher-value legal analysis, strategy and complex judgment calls.


However, faster output will expose new bottlenecks. Writing code has accelerated faster than human review and the bottleneck modern engineering teams face is in the review process. Legal teams will encounter a similar challenge. If AI produces more drafts, analyses and answers, but each requires the same amount of lawyer attention, work will get stuck in the review queue.


The answer is not more reviewers. It is deciding which work needs which kind of review, building confidence and trust in the work that should not need a lawyer in the loop, and creating systems that let lawyers apply their expertise and judgment where required.


That makes the next stage of adoption an organizational question, as well as a technological one.


## A shift to an AI-native operating model


We observe three types of operating models within in-house legal today.


-


**Manual:** Every task requires human initiation, execution, and review.


-


**AI-assisted:** Some tasks become faster and better, but the way the team operates remains largely unchanged.


-


**AI-native:** AI does more of the heavy lifting. Simpler tasks can be fully automated within approved guardrails, while more complex work begins with an AI-generated first pass. Lawyers direct the work, apply judgment where it is needed and remain accountable for the outcome.


That’s when traditional roles in a legal team start to change. Senior lawyers define the skills and set the standards that guide AI’s work. Junior lawyers and paralegals review AI outputs, Legal Operations designs workflows, and Compliance owners maintain the guidance and controls behind how the team operates.


Teams will make this transition at different speeds, building confidence as they go.[Mark Allen, Senior Director, Legal Innovation,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mark-allen-4a577314/) will explore this transition in more depth, including how to bring people with you and demonstrate value along the way.


## Tools that adapt to the work you need to do


Technology needs to support that transition. Today, one tool captures the request, another holds the contract, and a third tracks what happens next. Lawyers connect the steps and carry the context between them.


Yet many legal workflows share the same building blocks: agent capabilities, data and context, instructions that capture the team’s expertise, and tools to produce work and take action. Intake, contract drafting and regulatory monitoring combine these components in different ways.


We are building towards this at Legora: reusable capabilities that the Legora Agent brings together around a team’s work. As they become more capable and reliable, teams can assemble new workflows and apply their knowledge and policies to more use cases without starting from scratch.


The gains can compound: improving one shared capability can unlock several workflows at once. Better source verification, for example, can strengthen contract review, legal research and policy advice, expanding the range of work teams can confidently delegate.


[Adrian Parlow, VP Product,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adrianparlow/) will explore the product thinking behind this approach in a forthcoming blog.


## Bringing more work within reach


The impact of AI will become visible in what teams can make possible for their organizations: a project supported earlier, an agreement examined more closely, a question answered before it becomes an urgent problem. That is the opportunity behind legal work, without limits.


Over the coming weeks, we’ll explore this opportunity through the experiences of legal leaders, product releases and practical demonstrations. We’ll look at what teams can do today, how their ways of working are evolving and how to assess the value being created.


As today’s constraints begin to lift, what would yours make possible?
